_comment: Issue #1765: a rout keeps every man on his own slot, and the rally re-squares without scattering the block. Player Cavalry (uid 0, 18 horses on 5 files: 3 full ranks and a 3-horse short rank) starts facing south at (700, 500) and is quarter-turned right (E) at tick 12, so it faces west with a quarter-turn folded into its slot grid. A weak Infantry company (uid 1, 8 men) stands south of it. The enemy Cavalry (uid 2) charges the company, which breaks at tick 169; the contagion (12 morale off every friend within 140 wu) breaks the cavalry too, and uid 0 reads ROUTING from tick 170. The flight north snaps a quarter-turn more into the fold, a half-turn in all, and the cavalry rallies at tick 531, far from the fight. On main the rout dropped the fold, which swung the slot grid a quarter-turn about the anchor under the men: at tick 170 7 men's slots lay across the centreline from them and the farthest slot lay 160.0 wu sideways of its man (254.5 at tick 172), and the mean body-to-slot gap went from 0.0 to 180.4 wu (max 276.0). Here the rout moves no slot (0, 0.0, and a mean gap of 0.0). On main the rally then re-squared the quarter-turn fold the flight left, across the block (1 man across the centreline, 91.0 wu sideways, mean gap 42.7 to 115.4 wu, max 81.0 to 198.4). Here the troop rallies at tick 531 and pulls up with its heading held on its flight line, then re-squares at tick 863, once it has stopped: the fold is already a half-turn, so the heading does not turn, no slot moves sideways, and only the two short files' 6 horses step one rank (120 wu) forward, walking until about tick 1080 (mean body-to-slot gap 39.3 wu at tick 880, 22.0 at 960, 0.0 at 1080). The clip ends at tick 1100, as the enemy cavalry, which rides north after the fleeing company and through the troop's rear, reaches it; it attacks the troop from about tick 1136, after the clip. Expects after the re-square: at tick 864 no man's slot lies across the centreline and none lies sideways of him (the re-square moves slots in depth only; 1.0 wu allows the flight's 0.5 wu lateral lag plus the 0.5 wu float margin), and at tick 1080 the same with the walk done (0.5 wu, the float margin). On main, where the troop re-squared at the rally, the tick-864 lateral expect fails too (31.9 wu) and the other three pass. Expect tolerances: 0.5 wu at the rout is the float margin demos/README.md gives for slot_lateral_excess. At the rally the men carry a lateral lag from the flight (0.4 wu at tick 530 here), so 1.0 wu is the same 0.5 wu margin on top of a lag of up to 0.5 wu. Every expect below except the tick-8 pin and the two state claims fails on main.

shape_residual.reason: uid 2 is the enemy cavalry (48 horses, frontage 12). After the company breaks it marches north after it from about tick 400, and its horses fall behind their slots as it goes: mean body-to-slot gap 10.1 wu at tick 460, 22.7 at 500, 34.4 at 600 and 45.1 at 660. That is the long-pursuit drift tracked in #1716, and main does the same: over this script's own state ticks, to the clip's end at tick 1100, the shape_residual worst reads 48.59 on main 7d209821 and 54.74 here, against a 30 wu threshold; to tick 760 it read 41.03 and 40.29, so the rise is the longer chase. Measured 2026-10-11. uid 0 (the troop), on dense samples only: after its re-square at tick 863 the 6 horses of its two outer files walk one cavalry rank (120 wu) forward at the idle arrival pace and arrive by about tick 1080 (mean body-to-slot gap 39.3 wu at tick 880, 22.0 at 960, 0.0 at 1080). On 2-tick samples from tick 170 to tick 1100 its shape_residual reads 56.5 against the 30 wu threshold, and only between ticks 862 and 1080; outside that window it reads 8.85. On main 7d209821 it reads 116.3, from the rout on. Tracked in #1807 (men lag rebuilt slots at the idle arrival pace). Measured 2026-10-11.
